subject: Unified SEM with categorical data – Is this a correct approach?

messages.author: 160c9888b1a51028
messages.subject: Unified SEM with categorical data – Is this a correct approach?
parts:
Hello,

I am new to SEM and I am trying to modify the code from a published paper in the context of my categorical data: (https://quantdev.ssri.psu.edu/tutorials/socioemotional-dynamics-emotion-regulation-and-depressive-symptoms-person-specific-network). In this paper, they assumed their variables to be continuous as they ranged on a 1-100 scale.

For my research, I am trying to model the interaction between a mother and her infant using their individual affect time series (coded per sec) for a 5-min interaction. I have variables coded on specific Likert-type scales: MumPositiveAffect (0-3), MumNegativeAffect (0-3), MumNeutralAffect (0-1), InfPositiveAffect (0-1), InfNegativeAffect (0-1) and InfNeutralAffect (0-1). As these variables are highly correlated, I drop MumNeutralAffect and InfNeutralAffect as it does not provide any extra information and lavaan gives an error when I try to use all the variables.

I am interested in determining the lagged relationships between affects, so I start off with this null model which will later be modified by adding paths suggested by modification indices in lavaan:

Here the variables y5-y8 are MumPositiveAffect, MumNegativeAffect, InfPositiveAffect, InfNegativeAffect respectively and y1-y4 are the lagged variables of the same type at time-step (t-1). eta1-eta8 are the latent variables for each of the y1-y8 variables, so eta1-eta4 are latent variables for (t-1) timestep and eta5-eta8 are for the current (t) timestep.


This is my code:

###### Measurement model

eta1=~1 * y1

eta2=~1 * y2

eta3=~1 * y3

eta4=~1 * y4

eta5=~1 * y5

eta6=~1 * y6

eta7=~1 * y7

eta8=~1 * y8


##### Regression model

##### We do not want relationships of lagged (t-1) variables between themselves or to predict (t-1) variables

eta1~0*eta1\n   eta1~0*eta2\n    eta1~0*eta3\n    eta1~0*eta4\n    eta1~0*eta5\n    eta1~0*eta6\n   eta1~0*eta7\n   eta1~0*eta8

eta2~0*eta1\n   eta2~0*eta2\n   eta2~0*eta3\n   eta2~0*eta4\n   eta2~0*eta5\n   eta2~0*eta6\n   eta2~0*eta7\n   eta2~0*eta8

eta3~0*eta1\n   eta3~0*eta2\n   eta3~0*eta3\n   eta3~0*eta4\n   eta3~0*eta5\n   eta3~0*eta6\n   eta3~0*eta7\n   eta3~0*eta8

eta4~0*eta1\n   eta4~0*eta2\n   eta4~0*eta3\n   eta4~0*eta4\n   eta4~0*eta5\n   eta4~0*eta6\n   eta4~0*eta7\n   eta4~0*eta8


##### Auto-regressive part – predict (t) with (t-1)

eta5~eta1

eta6~eta2

eta7~eta3

eta8~eta4


##### Variance

eta1~~eta1\n   eta1~~eta2\n   eta1~~eta3\n  eta1~~eta4

eta2~~eta2\n   eta2~~eta3\n   eta2~~eta4

eta3~~eta3\n   eta3~~eta4

eta4~~eta4

eta5~~eta5

eta6~~eta6

eta7~~eta7

eta8~~eta8


fit <- lavaan::lavaan(model, data=data, model.type = "sem", estimator = "ML")


The following are the questions I have:

Questions

1. As the variables can both be predictors and predicted in this model (as modification indices adds new paths between eta5, eta6, eta7 and eta8), I am considering all variables as exogenous categorical here. The model works in this case. Is this correct?

2. I know that some of the variables are binary and/or ordinal, so I did try declaring all variables as “ordered” and using the same model with the WLSMV estimator. The model does not converge in that case. If this is the right way to do it, how should I get it to work?

3. I tried declaring only y5-y8 as endogenous ordered variables as they are the ones getting predicted, the model does not converge in that case too. I also tried declaring only the binary variables as endogenous ordered variables. It still does not converge. Is there any other way I should be approaching this problem or is the model that works with assuming all variables to be continuous is acceptable?


Thanks in advance,

Priyanka Khante

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Unified SEM with categorical data – Is this a correct approach?
parts: I am considering all variables as exogenous categorical here. The model works in this case. Is this correct?

No, they are all endogenous.  You are specifying them all as single-indicators of corresponding latent factors.  Not sure why that is necessary.  You also don't need to fix all those regressions to zero; they are zero by default, unless you explicitly free them.  Your syntax could be a lot simpler:
##### Auto-regressive part – predict (t) with (t-1)

y5 ~ y1
y6 ~ y2
y7 ~ y3
y8 ~ y4
2. I know that some of the variables are binary and/or ordinal
According to your description, all of them.  But no distributional assumptions are required of exogenous predictors, so you could avoid defining the unnecessary "eta"s.

so I did try declaring all variables as “ordered” and using the same model with the WLSMV estimator. The model does not converge in that case. If this is the right way to do it, how should I get it to work?

Use the sem() function to enable reasonable defaults.  Since you don't want to automatically estimate the residual covariances, you fix those to zero. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts: As all the variables are endogenous
y1-y4 are exogenous.
should I be declaring (y1-y8) as "ordered" or just the ones which are being predicted (y5-y8)? I
only the endogenous y5-y8
tried both combinations and the model is still not converging:

Don't specify parameters for exogenous variables. Those can be taken as given, rather than estimated.  Run this:

model <- '

## Regression model  
y5 ~ y1
y6 ~ y2
y7 ~ y3
y8 ~ y4

## fix residual covariances to zero, for some reason (why?)
y5 ~~ 0*y6 + 0*y7 + 0*y8
y6 ~~ 0*y7 + 0*y8
y7 ~~ 0*y8

'
fit <- sem(...) # automatically estimates residual variances, sets fixed.x=TRUE and conditional.x=TRUE
Could you please explain more about what you mean by this? - "Use the sem() function to enable reasonable defaults."
See Details in the ?sem help page.
